entries.clue: Long loaf listed by UNESCO in 2022
Coarse pate baked in the dish it is named for

Soft cheese from a region east of Paris
Flour cooked in butter to thicken a sauce

factCards.text: The artisanal know-how and culture of baguette bread was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2022.
factCards.sourceTitle: UNESCO — Representative List, artisanal know-how and culture of baguette bread (France, 2022)

factCards.text: Brie de Meaux and Brie de Melun both hold protected designation of origin status in the European Union.
factCards.sourceTitle: European Commission — eAmbrosia register of geographical indications

factCards.text: The croissant's laminated form is generally traced to Parisian bakers of the nineteenth century rather than to the Viennese kipferl it is often linked with; the connection is repeated widely but poorly documented.
factCards.sourceTitle: Oxford Companion to Food — croissant entry
